newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares dive on political concerns, off lows.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares dive on political concerns, off lows.

text.p: Istanbul shares dived on Thursday amid worries over the fate of Turkey's Islamist-led coalition government following a 6-1/2 day holiday, but rebounded from lows on late reaction buys, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,457, down 75 points, or 4.9 percent from the April 17 midday close of 1,532, but up slightly from a morning low of 1,420. Trade volume was 12.93 trillion lira ($96.4 million).
"Purchases in reaction to the sharp morning fall emerged in the afternoon. But the market will remain negative as long as political uneasiness continues," said Goksin Teker from Taib investment.

The market awaits Saturday's National Security Council (MGK) meeting amid rifts between the coalition government's Islamist and conservative wings following the secularist military's demands in the February 28 MGK meeting to combat rising Islamist activism.
"The index may drift sideways tomorrow but the market will set direction after the weekend news," said Nazmi Sarikaya from Dis securities.
